message.content: {"caption":"A workflow diagram shows archived coding agents being selected, modified, benchmarked, and added back to the archive.","description":"The left side shows a gray rounded panel labeled “Archive,” containing a branching tree of gray circular nodes. One node is red and labeled “parent”; a nearby label identifies it as a “Coding agent.” A yellow node labeled “child” is identified as the “New coding agent.” A thick black loop connects the archive to a green “Self-modify” button (with a wrench icon) and a blue “Evaluate on benchmark” button (with a magnifying-glass icon). The upper part of the loop is labeled “select,” indicating selection from the archive for modification; the lower part is labeled “add,” showing evaluated agents returning to the archive. On the right are two horizontal workflow lanes. In the upper lane, a repository icon and text “Coding agent’s own repo” plus “Self-improve instruction” lead right by an arrow to a circle labeled “Coding agent”; another right-pointing arrow leads to “Code Diff: Feature to improve itself,” beside a branching-code icon. A dashed curved arrow descends from this upper code-diff output toward the lower lane’s new-agent node. In the lower lane, a repository icon and “Task repo (e.g., GitHub repo)” plus “Task instruction (e.g., GitHub issue)” lead right by an arrow to a dashed circle labeled “New coding agent”; a further right-pointing arrow leads to “Code Diff: Solve task,” also beside a branching-code icon.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
